questions.question: CI/CD for network automation should emphasize:
options: Validated pipelines: lint/unit/integration, staged rollout, and fast rollback of bad configs/code
Pushing untested scripts straight to production fabric
questions.explanation: SysDE/NDE automation themes + SDM software lifecycle JD.

questions.question: A Network Core platform without SLIs/logs/traces is weak because:
options: You cannot detect, localize, or prove fixes when automation fails at scale
Observability is only for mobile apps
Metrics replace the need for ownership

questions.question: Best first automation target for a SysDE team supporting NDEs:
options: High-frequency, well-understood, error-prone toil with clear success checks
The rarest artisanal one-off with no validation path
Silent production mutations with no audit
questions.explanation: Invent and Simplify; Blind OpEx themes.

questions.question: After a tool causes a fabric impact, Highest Standards means:
options: Mitigate, then RCA with mechanism changes so the class of bug cannot recur
Restart once and close with no writeup
Blame the on-call personally and move on
questions.explanation: JD preferred: RCA and long-term fixes.

questions.question: As a hands-on SDM, Linux literacy in a SysDE incident means you can:
options: Follow host signals (CPU, disk, network, processes/logs) enough to challenge and unblock engineers
Memorize every man page without asking questions
questions.explanation: SysDE loops stress Linux triage; SDM must Dive Deep.

questions.question: Code review culture on Network Core software should optimize for:
options: Correctness, blast-radius safety, testability, and operability—not rubber stamps
questions.explanation: JD: code reviews, testing, deployment, post-launch monitoring.

questions.question: Deploying a change to fabric controllers / automation safely usually means:
options: Canary/small blast radius, health gates, automatic rollback, and clear ownership
Deploy Friday night with no on-call
Skip tests if CI is red
questions.explanation: Change safety transferred from network ops to software plane.

questions.question: Network automation jobs should be idempotent because:
options: Retries and partial failures are common; re-running must not corrupt intended state
Idempotency slows everything with no benefit

questions.question: Preferring APIs/events over SSH snowflake scripts helps Network Core scale by:
options: Making intent reviewable, testable, and automatable across a huge device/service fleet

questions.question: On-call for a Network Core software service should page on:
options: Customer/NDE-impacting symptoms and SLO burn—not every debug log line

questions.question: Capacity for a network control/ops platform includes:
options: Compute/storage/API quotas and dependency limits so growth doesn’t silently break change velocity
questions.explanation: Scalable systems experience from preferred quals.

questions.question: Security/compliance in Network Core tooling means:
options: Least privilege, audited changes, and not shipping secrets in repos or logs
Sharing root passwords in chat for speed

questions.question: Feature flags / config switches in fabric software help by:
options: Decoupling deploy from enablement and enabling rapid disable under impact

questions.question: When a downstream dependency (auth, queue, DB) flakes, Ownership looks like:
options: Protect customers with backoff/failover, escalate with data, and drive durable dependency fixes
Saying 'not my job' and closing the ticket

questions.question: Testing network automation well includes:
options: Unit tests plus simulated/lab devices or contract tests before production blast radius
Only testing in production on Friday

questions.question: Hands-on technical contribution as Network Core SDM should look like:
options: Unblocking design/reviews, pairing on hard incidents, and raising the technical bar—without becoming the sole coder
Writing 100% of production code alone forever
questions.explanation: JD: hands-on manager who still develops the team.
